proposed_from.topic: Generic characteristic-kernel cover-ratio recovery from one unknown-target perfect intervention per latent node. For every finite labeled DAG G and derivative-sign vector s, work in the relative product C2 topology on positive normalized C3 conditional mechanisms and perfect-intervention densities on [0,1], with faithful observational law and arbitrary shared C2 diffeomorphic mixing. With observable ratios R_i=dP^i/dP^0 and D_ji the Gaussian-kernel MMD between Law_0(R_i) and Law_j(R_i), prove that positive D_ji on every ancestral cover is open dense in every nonempty DAG/sign stratum. Derive the ancestral order from the ratio graph, componentwise coordinates by conditional ranks, the target assignment and exact faithful DAG by parent pruning, plus sample-split MMD confidence edges and conditional-CDF coordinate rates. Use the certified 1->2 plus isolated-3 witness with p2(y|x)=1+0.1(2x-1)(2y-1) and q_i(z)=4exp(4z)/(exp(4)-1). ROPES is the protocol consumer only after adopting a compliant positive common-support intervention generator. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Normalized affine interpolation toward a sparse edge witness preserves normalization globally and positivity, fixed derivative signs, and faithfulness locally. The direct-edge second-moment contrast is analytic and nonzero at the endpoint, so its zeros are isolated; this derives open-dense direct-edge separation and therefore characteristic-kernel cover separation. The sparse witness has an analytic moment gap above 3e-4 and Gaussian MMD above 5e-8. Exact faithful cancellation families, isolated nodes, multiple roots, forks, colliders, opposite parent effects, redundant edges, and disconnected admissibility strata were checked; no current-literature collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform conditional-CDF coordinate rates when both response thresholds and conditioning covariates are estimated log-density ratios on an explicitly bounded Holder subclass. EARLY KILL TEST: Independently verify the analytic moment-integral identity along the normalized affine path from the exact cancellation example to the sparse witness, including preservation of finite positive faithfulness and derivative-sign margins near its start. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_crl_coverratio_mmd_genericity.md.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: {"published_axis":"The closest nonparametric invertible-mixing result, von Kugelgen et al. (2023), proves the one-intervention theorem only for two latents and uses two interventions per node in arbitrary dimension. Jiang and Aragam (2023, Theorem 3.4) attain one intervention per hidden variable on the orthogonal measurement-model axis, under marginal-independence graphical conditions and only up to isolated latent edges. Ahuja et al. (2023, Theorem 5.3) attain one-per-latent perfect-do coordinate recovery on the orthogonal finite-degree polynomial-mixing and support-geometry axis, without recovering the DAG. Buchholz et al. (2023, Theorem 1) attain unknown-target single-node recovery under arbitrary nonlinear mixing on the orthogonal linear Gaussian latent-SCM axis. The new delta is an observable environment-label ratio graph whose transitive closure supplies the missing order for every finite DAG with smooth positive compact-support nonparametric mechanisms under shared diffeomorphic mixing, together with component recovery and open-dense cover separation inside each nonempty faithful derivative-sign stratum; no subsumption of the Jiang--Aragam, Ahuja, or Buchholz regimes is claimed.","repo_axis":"No bounded-catalogue proposal studies cover-ratio MMD genericity under arbitrary shared diffeomorphic mixing. The core makes the population recovery map the headline, treats fixed-bandwidth confidence edges conditionally on an explicit first-stage error event, and exposes generated conditional-rank rates as a first-class open question."}

seed_details.one_line: Prove that positive characteristic-kernel discrepancy on every ancestral cover is open dense in every nonempty faithful sign stratum and that the resulting ratio graph recovers order, coordinates, targets, and the exact DAG.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Von Kugelgen et al. (2023, Section 7) explicitly conjecture arbitrary-dimensional identification from one perfect intervention per node and identify the target-misalignment combinatorics as the obstacle.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace enumeration of the \(n!-1\) target permutations by an observable graph on environment labels, and replace an assumed bivariate witness by normalized-kernel interpolation plus an analytic direct-edge moment contrast.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is immediate from the bivariate witness argument of von Kugelgen et al. combined with ordinary faithfulness genericity.
seed_details.rebuttal: The bivariate proof has no observable arbitrary-dimensional order certificate, and ordinary faithfulness interpolation does not establish noncancellation of a mechanism-dependent ratio under two surgically related laws; the analytic identity and sparse endpoint are the missing steps.

seed_details.one_line: Characterize exactly when an ancestral cover is invisible to every ratio-law test and whether the cancellation set is a stratified analytic hypersurface.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Von Kugelgen et al. (2023, equation (3.2) and Remark 3.3) impose a witness-function genericity condition but do not characterize its failure set.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After deriving equality of all ratio-law expectations, analyze the nonlinear pushforward equality as an operator equation rather than contradicting it with an assumed witness.
seed_details.referee_objection: The condition is tautologically equality of two pushforward laws and therefore has no theorem-level content.
seed_details.rebuttal: A viable result would need a finite or differential characterization and a necessity construction over a nondegenerate region; that characterization is not supplied by the tautology.
seed_details.status: dropped after Step 1 because no finite characterization emerged beyond the pushforward equality

seed_details.one_line: Derive the uniform rate and asymptotic-linear expansion of conditional ranks when the response threshold and all conditioning coordinates are cross-fitted log-density ratios.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Xie (2023, Theorems 1--3) treats observed thresholds and covariates, whereas Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012, Theorem 1) treats generated kernel arguments for smooth regression outcomes.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Linearize boundary crossings of the discontinuous indicator simultaneously with perturbations of the local-linear design matrix caused by generated conditioning coordinates.
seed_details.referee_objection: Sample splitting and the ordinary generated-regressor expansion make the result routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: Sample splitting removes own-observation dependence but does not control a generated response threshold, whose first-stage error changes indicator membership and the empirical-process index set.
seed_details.status: survived as the principal open-ended inference question

seed_details.one_line: Match lower and upper sample-complexity bounds for ancestral-order recovery when the minimum cover MMD shrinks and ratios are estimated on independent folds.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Gretton et al. (2012) and Schrab et al. (2023) calibrate MMD for observed inputs, not graph-wide tests of learned likelihood-ratio values.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Couple a least-favorable opposite-order SCM path to the stochastic expansion of a learned-ratio MMD process shared across all ordered edges.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is a union bound over standard MMD tests.
seed_details.rebuttal: A union bound gives fixed-margin consistency but neither the local converse nor the interaction between vanishing structural separation and first-stage ratio error.
seed_details.status: survived as a follow-on, not chosen because the attainable nonlinear ratio learner is unresolved

seed_details.one_line: Characterize the maximal recoverable nonlinear latent equivalence class under one unknown-target soft atomic intervention per node.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Jaber et al. (2020, Theorems 1--3) give a sound-and-complete unknown-target soft-intervention equivalence class for observed variables, while von Kugelgen et al. (2023, Section 7) ask for weaker nonparametric CRL notions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Lift invariance equivalence from observed nodes to latent coordinate sigma-fields while quotienting parent-dependent representation transformations.
seed_details.referee_objection: Var\i{}c\i{} et al. already identify latents up to mixing with parents under soft interventions.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their score-support result is sufficient and transformation-specific; it is not a sound-and-complete maximal equivalence-class characterization with unknown target assignments.
seed_details.status: dropped after Step 1 because the latent completeness construction is not yet sufficiently bounded for a first version

seed_details.one_line: Derive an observable regime in which score-change and ratio-law causal-representation decoders agree, and identify the boundary where only one remains informative.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Var\i{}c\i{} et al. (2025, Theorem 29) use score-change support under two interventions per node for general transformations, while the ratio method uses one perfect intervention and a known observational law.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Express both support certificates as derivatives of the same observed log-density-ratio family before comparing their zero sets.
seed_details.referee_objection: The score is merely the derivative of the log ratio, so equivalence is immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection largely holds because integration constants and environment pairing do not create a sufficiently sharp new frontier in the present perfect-intervention model.

seed_details.one_line: Replace third-order sufficient-change conditions in general-environment CRL by ratio-law ordering on additive-Gaussian and heteroscedastic latent models.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Ng et al. (2025, Theorems 1--2) recover sinks through third derivatives and sufficient-change rank conditions under general environments.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the third-derivative sink induction by a cross-environment likelihood-ratio law whose nonzero edges reveal ancestry.
seed_details.referee_objection: Perfect interventions are less general than the environments of Ng et al., so this is not a relaxation of their theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds as a comparator claim; the models trade environment generality for mechanism generality, leaving no clean strict extension on that anchor alone.

seed_details.one_line: Construct graph-wide familywise-valid learned-ratio MMD confidence edges, optionally aggregating bandwidths without splitting the evaluation fold.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Schrab et al. (2023, main minimax theorem and Section 6) aggregate observed-sample MMD tests, while the ratio graph reuses fitted ratios and the observational evaluation sample across edges.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Condition on the training fold, bound feature-map perturbations from fitted ratios, and calibrate the maximum over shared graph edges rather than one two-sample statistic.
seed_details.referee_objection: Conditional on the fitted ratios, bounded differences and a union bound settle the result.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection lands for fixed Gaussian bandwidth, so that result is retained only as an inference rung; adaptive aggregation and a data-driven first-stage radius remain separate open content.

proposed_from.literature_map: Von Kugelgen et al. (2023, Theorems 3.2 and 3.4, Appendix C.2, and Section 7) identify two nonparametric latents from one unknown-target perfect intervention per node under a ratio-law witness condition, but use two interventions per node for arbitrary dimension and explicitly leave the one-per-node extension open. Wendong et al. (2023, Theorem 4.2) recover components from one perfect intervention per node when the DAG and intervention alignment are supplied. Var\i{}c\i{} et al. (2025, Theorem 29) use two uncoupled hard interventions per node for general transformations; their one-intervention result is confined to linear mixing. Ng et al. (2025, Theorems 1 and 2 and Appendices D--E) recover a DAG under nonparametric mixing from derivative-rich general environments by imposing additive-Gaussian or heteroscedastic latent mechanisms. Boeken, Forr\'e, and Mooij (2026, Definition 4 and Lemmas 3--4) interpolate normalized conditional kernels to prove typical faithfulness, but do not control surgically related likelihood-ratio laws. Yao et al. (2025, Assumption D.1 and Corollary D.1) use a supplied topological target order, which is the object recovered here. Gretton et al. (2012, Theorems 5, 7, and 13) establish characteristic-kernel two-sample separation and MMD concentration for observed inputs. Xie (2023, Theorems 1--3) gives uniform local-linear conditional-CDF expansions for observed responses and covariates, while Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012, Theorem 1) linearize kernel regression with generated covariates but not generated indicator thresholds. Lee, Jin, and Aragam (2026, Theorems 4.6--4.7) give finite-sample graph and representation recovery for linear factor models with multi-node interventions, leaving the nonlinear learned-ratio setting distinct. No inspected source combines arbitrary-dimensional one-per-node nonparametric identification, an observable ratio-order certificate, and open-dense verification of that certificate inside each faithful derivative-sign stratum.
